slides.headline: HERTZ-AI JUST OPEN-SOURCED AN AI OPERATING SYSTEM DESIGNED SO FRONTIER MODELS NEVER NEED A DATACENTER AGAIN
slides.subline: BIG TECH BUILT THE CLOUD TO STOP THIS

slides.headline: THE OS RUNNING FRONTIER AI ON LOCAL HARDWARE
slides.body: HART OS—full name Hevolve Hive Agentic Runtime OS—is an open-source operating system built ground-up to run frontier AI models without cloud dependency. The hertz-ai team architected every layer: a local agent ledger, a persistent memory module, a voice interface, and a security layer called Hevolve Armor. The entire stack runs on NixOS with a developer SDK already shipped

slides.headline: 9 MODULES THAT REPLACE THE CLOUD
slides.body: HART OS ships with 9 open-source modules: a core runtime, a native agent ledger for action tracking, a compositor for UI, a memory system, speech and audio support, Hevolve Armor security, an integrations layer, a developer SDK, and full NixOS configuration. The hart_sdk and demo modules are already live, letting any developer build on the stack today. Every component is open-source on GitHub

slides.headline: HOW IT KILLS THE DATACENTER BILL
slides.body: Instead of routing agent actions to a cloud API, HART OS runs AI orchestration at the OS level—every decision stays on local hardware. The agent ledger logs actions locally; the memory module holds persistent context without remote storage; the compositor handles display without a server call. The result: a full agentic runtime with zero API fees and no data leaving the device

slides.headline: THE 9 CONTRIBUTORS BETTING THE CLOUD ERA IS OVER
slides.body: Hertz-ai launched HART OS publicly on Hacker News with just 9 contributors, 15 GitHub stars, and 2 forks—the kind of early signal that precedes category-defining projects. The team's thesis, encoded in the name "Hevolve Hive", is that AI agents belong in a local hive of hardware, not rented cloud nodes. They shipped a working demo, a full SDK, and complete documentation at launch

slides.headline: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN AI LEAVES THE CLOUD
slides.body: Every major AI lab today relies on cloud infrastructure—the assumption powering the entire industry is that frontier models need someone else's hardware. HART OS is the first open-source OS to directly challenge that assumption, putting the full agentic runtime on local machines. If the architecture scales, the cloud AI infrastructure layer—today's fastest-growing enterprise cost center—becomes optional, not mandatory

slides.headline: WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOUR BUSINESS
slides.body: Cloud AI costs are the fastest-growing line item for businesses running AI at scale—and local AI OS infrastructure like HART OS points to a future where your stack runs on hardware you own, with zero API fees and no data leaving your network. Companies in legal, medical, and finance with strict data-residency rules stand to benefit first. The question isn't whether local AI infrastructure arrives—it's whether your business is ready when it does
